feedback.worked_solution:
According to the sum and constant multiple rules, we can compute the required limit as follows:

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,2}(7f(x)+8g(x)-2{x}^{3})=7{lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)+8{lim}_{x\to \,2}g(x)-2{lim}_{x\to \,2}{x}^{3}
$$

  

The above equation assumes that ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to \,2}g(x)$ both exist.

In part 5, we found that ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)=4,$ and from part 3, we found ${lim}_{x\to \,2}g(x)=-1.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,2}(7f(x)+8g(x)-2{x}^{3}) & =7{lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)+8{lim}_{x\to \,2}g(x)-2{lim}_{x\to \,2}{x}^{3} \\  & =7\cdot 4+8\cdot (-1)-2\cdot {2}^{3} \\  & =28-8-16 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
